name: Frecuencia de apellidos (Instituto Nacional de Estadística)
note: Spanish surnames, which nothing else here could supply. INE publishes given names as
xlsx and surnames only as a legacy `.xls` — an OLE2 container full of BIFF8 records,
which no tool a build machine is guaranteed to have will convert. `libreoffice`,
`ssconvert` and `catdoc` are all real answers and none of them is installed anywhere,
so `CFB` and `XLS` read it directly. See those files for why that was the cheaper risk.
Two sheets, split by how many people hold the surname. Only the first is read: 27,661
surnames held by 100 or more. The second carries 20 to 99, which is a long tail a
weighted draw would reach about never and 58,000 more rows in every locale module.
The count taken is `Ambos apellidos` — how many people carry the surname in either
position. Spain gives everyone two, and counting only first surnames would halve the
weight of every name that is commoner as a mother's than as a father's.
Before this, `es` had INE's given names and no surnames at all, so `fullName()` was
composed entirely in English rather than pairing María with a US Census surname — the
coherence rule doing its job over data that was not there.
